subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hybridization of carbon in benzene?
explain: Each carbon in benzene is sp² hybridized with one unhybridized p orbital forming π system.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which alkane is most reactive toward free radical halogenation?
explain: Tertiary H is most reactive; 2-methylpropane has a tertiary carbon giving most stable 3° radical.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Markovnikov's rule: HX adds to alkene such that H goes to carbon with?
explain: H attaches to carbon bearing more H atoms (less substituted C), giving more stable carbocation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of 2-butene followed by reductive workup gives?
explain: 2-Butene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) cleaves at double bond giving two CH₃CHO (ethanal) molecules.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Lindlar's catalyst converts alkynes to?
explain: Lindlar's catalyst (Pd/CaCO₃/quinoline) gives syn addition of H₂ → cis-alkene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Birch reduction of benzene uses Na in liquid NH₃ + alcohol to give?
explain: Birch reduction gives 1,4-cyclohexadiene; substituent effects determine which positions remain unsaturated.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The IUPAC name of CH₃-C≡C-CH₃ is?
explain: Triple bond between C2 and C3 in a 4-carbon chain → 2-Butyne (But-2-yne).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Terminal alkynes are acidic (pKa ≈ 25) because the C–H bond is?
explain: sp carbon has 50% s-character; higher s-character → closer to nucleus → more acidic C–H.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which reagent converts alkene to vicinal diol (syn addition)?
explain: OsO₄ gives syn dihydroxylation forming cis-diol; cold dilute KMnO₄ also gives syn diol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Electrophilic substitution on toluene: -CH₃ directs incoming group to?
explain: -CH₃ is ortho/para director (electron-donating by hyperconjugation) in EAS.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nitration of benzene uses a mixture of?
explain: Mixed acid (HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄) generates nitronium ion (NO₂⁺) the electrophile.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Free radical addition of HBr to propene (peroxide effect) gives?
explain: Peroxide effect causes anti-Markovnikov addition; Br goes to terminal (less substituted) carbon.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of alkyne with water (H₂SO₄/HgSO₄) gives?
explain: Acid-catalysed hydration of alkynes gives enol which tautomerises to carbonyl compound.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Heat of combustion order among CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈ per mole?
explain: Heat of combustion per mole increases with increasing number of carbons in alkanes.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Wurtz reaction uses alkyl halide + Na to give?
explain: Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides using Na metal to form a higher symmetrical alkane.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which of these is NOT aromatic by Hückel's rule (4n+2 π e⁻)?
explain: Cyclobutadiene has 4π electrons (4n, n=1) → antiaromatic, not aromatic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Baeyer's test (cold dilute KMnO₄) turns from purple to?
explain: Alkenes decolourise purple KMnO₄; MnO₂ brown precipitate forms, confirming unsaturation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Stability order of carbocations: 3° vs 2° vs 1° vs CH₃⁺?
explain: More alkyl groups donate electrons by hyperconjugation/induction, stabilising the carbocation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate gives?
explain: Electrolysis of CH₃COONa → at anode: 2CH₃COO⁻ → C₂H₆ + 2CO₂ (Kolbe's synthesis).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: E/Z isomerism in alkenes requires each double-bond carbon to have?
explain: Geometric isomerism exists when each sp² carbon carries two different substituents.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene uses?
explain: Alkyl halide + Lewis acid AlCl₃ generates carbocation electrophile for EAS alkylation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which hydrocarbon gives a white precipitate with ammoniacal AgNO₃?
explain: Terminal alkynes react with AgNO₃/NH₃ to form silver acetylide (white ppt); confirms acidic C–H.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane with alc. KOH gives major product by?
explain: Saytzeff's rule: elimination gives more substituted (stable) alkene as the major product.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Number of σ bonds in ethyne (HC≡CH)?
explain: Ethyne: 2 C–H σ bonds + 1 C–C σ bond = 3 σ bonds; triple bond has 1σ + 2π.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: -NO₂ group on benzene ring is a?
explain: -NO₂ is strongly electron-withdrawing (–M effect), making ring less reactive and meta-directing.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Combustion of methane: products are?
explain: Complete combustion of any alkane gives CO₂ and H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hybridization of each carbon in ethene (C₂H₄)?
explain: Each carbon in ethene forms a double bond; it is sp² hybridized with one π bond.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ozonolysis of ethene with oxidative workup gives?
explain: Oxidative ozonolysis of ethene gives formic acid (HCOOH) from each –CH₂– fragment.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which species is the electrophile in benzene nitration?
explain: HNO₃ + H₂SO₄ generates NO₂⁺ (nitronium ion), the active electrophile in nitration.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Anti-addition of Br₂ to alkene proceeds via?
explain: Br₂ addition forms a cyclic bromonium ion intermediate, giving anti (trans) addition product.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of alkyne with excess Br₂ (2 mol) gives?
explain: Two moles of Br₂ add across the triple bond to give a tetrabromoalkane.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The general formula of cycloalkanes is?
explain: Cycloalkanes have one ring (one degree of unsaturation), giving formula CₙH₂ₙ.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Smallest cycloalkane with maximum angle strain is?
explain: Cyclopropane has 60° bond angles vs 109.5° ideal, giving maximum Baeyer (angle) strain.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Cyclohexane's most stable conformation is?
explain: Chair conformation of cyclohexane has no angle or torsional strain; most stable.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Axial vs equatorial in cyclohexane: bulky groups prefer?
explain: Equatorial position avoids 1,3-diaxial interactions, so bulky groups prefer equatorial.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Friedel-Crafts acylation product on benzene is?
explain: Acyl halide + AlCl₃ generates acylium ion (RCO⁺) which gives aryl ketone (PhCOR).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Sulfonation of benzene with fuming H₂SO₄ is?
explain: Benzene sulfonation is reversible; desulfonation occurs with steam/dilute acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which group makes benzene ring MORE reactive toward EAS?
explain: -OH donates electrons by resonance (+M effect), activating the ring toward EAS.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Halogens on benzene ring are classified as?
explain: Halogens withdraw electrons (-I) deactivating ring but direct o/p via lone pair resonance.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Degree of unsaturation (DoU) for C₆H₆ is?
explain: DoU = (2×6+2−6)/2 = 8/2 = 4 (3 double bonds + 1 ring for benzene).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which alkyl halide formation is favoured by HX + alkene via Markovnikov?
explain: H⁺ adds to CH₂ (less substituted C), Br⁻ adds to CH₃CH⁺–CH₃ giving 2-bromopropane.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Pyrolysis (cracking) of alkanes is also called?
explain: Heating alkanes at high temperature breaks C–C bonds (thermal cracking) giving smaller fragments.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Relative reactivity of halogens in free-radical substitution of alkanes?
explain: Reactivity order: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂; I₂ is too slow/endothermic to be useful.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Selectivity in free-radical halogenation: which is more selective?
explain: Br• is more selective than Cl• because it is less reactive; selectivity ∝ 1/reactivity.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The C–C bond in ethane allows what kind of motion?
explain: Single σ bond in ethane allows free rotation; double bonds restrict rotation due to π bond.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Most stable conformation of ethane is?
explain: Staggered conformation minimizes torsional strain; eclipsed is least stable.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Vinyl carbocation (CH₂=CH⁺) stability compared to 1° alkyl carbocation?
explain: Vinyl cation is sp hybridized; highly unstable, less stable than even 1° carbocation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which compound shows geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
explain: 2-Butene has two different groups on each sp² carbon; shows cis/trans isomerism.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Addition of HOCl to alkene gives?
explain: HOCl adds via Cl⁺ (electrophile); OH and Cl add anti giving a chlorohydrin.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzene does NOT easily undergo addition reactions because?
explain: Addition would disrupt the delocalized π system and destroy aromaticity (extra stability ~36 kcal/mol).
